title: Primary 1 Mathematics — Foundational Numbers and Shapes
subject: Mathematics
description: A six-lesson supplementary introductory mathematics sequence; not a full term, formal assessment or verified NERDC scheme.
prerequisites: Facilitator checks appropriateness and provides large drawn objects or paper
Learners may explain by speech, pointing, drawing or a familiar language

lessons.title: Numbers Around Us
lessons.learningObjective: Identify, read and represent whole numbers from 0 to 20.
lessons.content:
Numbers Around Us

Learning objective: Identify, read and represent whole numbers from 0 to 20.

Teacher models: Explain the idea with drawings, invite a learner to describe the process, then ask learners to attempt the guided task.

Guided task: Draw 4 books and 3 cups. Count each set, then count all objects.

Check: How many objects altogether?

Expected response: 7. Four plus three equals seven.

Independent practice: Draw 5 windows and 2 doors; how many shapes in all?

Practice guidance: 7.

Facilitator note: Allow drawn, oral or pointed responses; adapt quantities to the learner's current skills without treating the task as a clinical or formal attainment test. Check understanding privately, avoid public rankings, and do not collect student identifiers or photographs.

lessons.title: Comparing Groups
lessons.learningObjective: Compare two sets using more, fewer, and equal.
lessons.content:
Comparing Groups

Learning objective: Compare two sets using more, fewer, and equal.

Teacher models: Explain the idea with drawings, invite a learner to describe the process, then ask learners to attempt the guided task.

Guided task: Draw seven large circles and five squares. Match them in pairs.

Check: Which set has more and how many more?

Expected response: Circles; two more.

Independent practice: Draw 6 stars and 4 triangles. Compare.

Practice guidance: Stars have two more.

Facilitator note: Allow drawn, oral or pointed responses; adapt quantities to the learner's current skills without treating the task as a clinical or formal attainment test. Check understanding privately, avoid public rankings, and do not collect student identifiers or photographs.

lessons.title: Adding With Pictures
lessons.content:
Adding With Pictures

Learning objective: Model addition within 20 using pictures.

Teacher models: Explain the idea with drawings, invite a learner to describe the process, then ask learners to attempt the guided task.

Guided task: Draw six pencils, then draw four more. Count the combined group.

Check: What is 6 + 4?

Expected response: 10.

Independent practice: Draw 8 leaves then 3 leaves; add.

Practice guidance: 11.

Facilitator note: Allow drawn, oral or pointed responses; adapt quantities to the learner's current skills without treating the task as a clinical or formal attainment test. Check understanding privately, avoid public rankings, and do not collect student identifiers or photographs.
lessons.activity: Draw six pencils, then draw four more. Count the combined group.

lessons.title: Taking Away
lessons.content:
Taking Away

Learning objective: Model subtraction using crossed-out drawings.

Teacher models: Explain the idea with drawings, invite a learner to describe the process, then ask learners to attempt the guided task.

Guided task: Draw 9 balls, cross out 3, and count what remains.

Check: What is 9 − 3?

Expected response: 6.

Independent practice: Draw 12 mango pictures, cross out 5.

Practice guidance: 7 remain.

Facilitator note: Allow drawn, oral or pointed responses; adapt quantities to the learner's current skills without treating the task as a clinical or formal attainment test. Check understanding privately, avoid public rankings, and do not collect student identifiers or photographs.

lessons.title: Shapes in Everyday Life
lessons.learningObjective: Recognise basic two-dimensional shapes without needing formal measurements.
lessons.content:
Shapes in Everyday Life

Learning objective: Recognise basic two-dimensional shapes without needing formal measurements.

Teacher models: Explain the idea with drawings, invite a learner to describe the process, then ask learners to attempt the guided task.

Guided task: Draw a door, a plate and a roof outline; discuss their approximate shapes.

Check: Which often resembles a rectangle, a door or a plate?

Expected response: A door. A plate often resembles a circle.

Independent practice: Draw one rectangle, circle and triangle and identify an object resembling each.

Practice guidance: Responses vary; check shape features.

Facilitator note: Allow drawn, oral or pointed responses; adapt quantities to the learner's current skills without treating the task as a clinical or formal attainment test. Check understanding privately, avoid public rankings, and do not collect student identifiers or photographs.

lessons.title: Checking Our Thinking
lessons.learningObjective: Explain and check an addition or subtraction method using a drawing.
lessons.content:
Checking Our Thinking

Learning objective: Explain and check an addition or subtraction method using a drawing.

Teacher models: Explain the idea with drawings, invite a learner to describe the process, then ask learners to attempt the guided task.

Guided task: A class has 5 storybooks and adds 4; draw, count and confirm by recounting.

Check: How many books? How can we check?

Expected response: 9. Count all objects or start at five and count four more.

Independent practice: Draw 10 books, give away 2 and explain the remainder.

Practice guidance: 8.

Facilitator note: Allow drawn, oral or pointed responses; adapt quantities to the learner's current skills without treating the task as a clinical or formal attainment test. Check understanding privately, avoid public rankings, and do not collect student identifiers or photographs.
